stories.title: Organisation Release: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
stories.summary: Hubble and Webb have imaged a dusty pillar nicknamed the Cat's Head Nebula inside the Carina Nebula, about 7,500 light-years from Earth. In visible light the dust looks opaque, but Webb's infrared images see through much of it, exposing embedded young stars and warm dust. Ultraviolet radiation from nearby massive stars ionises and heats the pillar's edges, slowly evaporating gas and shaping where new stars can form.

stories.title: New converter could bridge light wavelength gap in quantum communications
stories.summary: Researchers have built a new converter that could help overcome a mismatch in light wavelengths within quantum networks. These networks link stationary qubits, such as quantum information stored in trapped ions, by sending single photons along optical fibres. Matching wavelengths between the parts of the network could make secure quantum links more practical. It also shows the photon model of light, where each particle carries energy set by its wavelength, being used in real technology.

stories.title: Single X-ray pulse reveals plasma nanostructures across scales with one camera
stories.summary: Researchers used a single X-ray pulse and one camera to capture nanoscale structures of many different sizes inside a plasma. In plasmas, small disturbances can grow through instabilities, while turbulence passes energy between large and small structures, shaping how the plasma moves and carries energy. Imaging these features together could help laser-plasma experiments, fusion energy research and astrophysics.

stories.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe
stories.summary: Astronomers studied 2,884 exploding stars, or supernovae, and found new evidence that dark energy, which drives the accelerating expansion of the universe, might not stay constant over time. Because these explosions act as standard candles for measuring distance, they let researchers trace how expansion has changed. If confirmed, the result would challenge a central assumption of the standard cosmological model.

stories.title: Webb Captures Stellar Jets
stories.summary: Infrared images from the James Webb Space Telescope show many young stars and still-forming protostars inside the star-forming cloud NGC 7129. The picture separates warm hydrogen in single-atom form from cooler hydrogen bound into molecules, which jets from buried protostars have struck and heated. Such observations help astronomers study how collapsing gas clouds give rise to new stars.

stories.title: Infrared light overcomes mirror coating obstacle in gravitational wave detector upgrades
stories.summary: Researchers have developed and tested a new locking method for gravitational wave detectors that will advance the discovery of distant black holes and neutron stars colliding.
